customer.business: GradTrail, a free, open-source, self-hosted job-search and application workspace
customer.target: Students, recent graduates, and early-career developers worldwide looking for internships and entry-level technical roles
customer.where: Worldwide; source and country coverage varies by configured job provider

behaviours.name: Multi-board checker
behaviours.how: Checks several job boards, employer career pages, and social posts each week.

behaviours.name: Eligibility-first applicant
behaviours.how: Checks experience level, location, work authorization, degree, and deadline before applying.

behaviours.name: Project-led candidate
behaviours.how: Uses personal projects, coursework, and open-source work to demonstrate skills.

behaviours.name: Application organizer
behaviours.how: Applies to several roles and tracks stages, deadlines, and follow-ups in a spreadsheet.

behaviours.name: Privacy-conscious self-hoster
behaviours.how: Prefers keeping application data on a system they control, but weighs setup effort carefully.

behaviours.name: Trust and freshness checker
behaviours.how: Checks original links, dates, employer identity, and whether an opening is still active.

behaviours.name: Referral-network builder
behaviours.how: Uses alumni, developer communities, and referrals to find roles outside large job boards.

objections: I already use LinkedIn, Indeed, company career pages, or student job boards; why add another tool?
Will the configured sources actually cover roles and countries I care about?
Are the posting dates, links, and application deadlines clear and current?
Self-hosting a database and configuring provider keys sounds difficult.
Could API, AI, or hosting costs make a free app expensive to use?
Will AI drafts use my projects accurately without inventing experience?
Can I use it on my laptop without high memory or hardware requirements?
I do not want to upload private application or resume data to an unknown service.
habits: You check opportunities between classes, after work, or on weekends, often from a laptop with limited memory.
You save roles from several countries and boards, then lose track of which ones need a follow-up.
You rely on projects and coursework because your formal work history is short.
You want to see the employer's original post and check eligibility before spending time applying.
You prefer a no-cost tool but may tolerate setup if it gives you control over your data.

pitch:
GradTrail is a free, open-source, self-hosted job-search and application workspace for students and early-career developers worldwide.
On Windows, macOS, or Linux, the setup script checks Docker, asks you to choose a sign-in password, creates local secrets, and starts GradTrail on your machine.
Start searching with keyless sources such as FreeHire, Remote OK, and student feeds; add other providers for wider or regional coverage. Dates and country coverage depend on the source, and every result links to its original post.
Track applications and deadlines, and draft resumes from your profile and projects. AI is optional; drafts use profile facts and stay yours to review. Other provider or hosting costs may apply; no hosted plan is offered.
